external_entities.name: sensor node
external_entities.description: A deployed sensor installed on a customer site that publishes readings and polls for firmware images.
external_entities.source_excerpt: We have a few thousand sensor nodes installed on customer sites.
external_entities.notes: A technician can be standing next to one with a laptop.

external_entities.name: field technician
external_entities.description: A technician who services sensor nodes over a local serial console.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Field technicians service nodes over a local serial console.

external_entities.name: fleet operator
external_entities.description: An operator who views telemetry dashboards from the corporate network.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Our own fleet operators look at dashboards over BigQuery from the corporate network

processes.name: device gateway
processes.description: An MQTT broker running on GKE that accepts sensor readings, checks devices against the device registry, and forwards accepted readings.
processes.source_excerpt: the device gateway, which is an MQTT broker we run on GKE

processes.name: telemetry normalizer
processes.description: A Python consumer in the analytics network that picks up readings and writes them to the telemetry lake.
processes.source_excerpt: the telemetry normalizer, a Python consumer in our analytics network

processes.name: dashboard
processes.description: A dashboard used by fleet operators to view telemetry over BigQuery.
processes.source_excerpt: fleet operators look at dashboards over BigQuery

data_stores.name: device registry
data_stores.description: A Firestore registry used to check the sensor key and determine which customer a node belongs to.
data_stores.source_excerpt: a device registry (Firestore) to check the key and to find out which customer the node belongs to

data_stores.name: Pub/Sub
data_stores.description: A Pub/Sub service carrying readings forwarded by the device gateway for pickup by the telemetry normalizer.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Readings the gateway accepts are forwarded onto Pub/Sub

data_stores.name: telemetry lake
data_stores.description: A BigQuery data store containing readings, site addresses, and occupancy patterns; it is customer data.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The lake has site addresses and occupancy patterns in it, so it is customer data.

data_stores.name: Cloud Storage bucket
data_stores.description: A bucket containing firmware images that sensor nodes poll and install; it is publicly readable.
data_stores.source_excerpt: nodes poll a Cloud Storage bucket for a new image

data_flows.name: publish readings
data_flows.description: Sensor nodes publish readings to the device gateway.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Each node publishes readings over MQTT to the device gateway

data_flows.name: look up device
data_flows.description: The device gateway looks up a device in the device registry to check its key and customer association.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The gateway looks up the device in a device registry (Firestore) to check the key and to find out which customer the node belongs to.

data_flows.name: forward readings
data_flows.description: The device gateway forwards accepted readings onto Pub/Sub.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Readings the gateway accepts are forwarded onto Pub/Sub

data_flows.name: pick up readings
data_flows.description: The telemetry normalizer picks up readings from Pub/Sub.
data_flows.source_excerpt: picked up by the telemetry normalizer

data_flows.name: write readings
data_flows.description: The telemetry normalizer writes readings into the telemetry lake.
data_flows.source_excerpt: which writes them into the telemetry lake in BigQuery

data_flows.name: poll image
data_flows.description: Sensor nodes poll the Cloud Storage bucket for a firmware image.
data_flows.source_excerpt: nodes poll a Cloud Storage bucket for a new image

data_flows.name: service console
data_flows.description: Field technicians service sensor nodes over a local serial console.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Field technicians service nodes over a local serial console.
data_flows.notes: The source does not state what authentication the console has, if any.

data_flows.name: view dashboards
data_flows.description: Fleet operators view dashboards while signed in with company SSO.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Our own fleet operators look at dashboards over BigQuery from the corporate network, signed in with company SSO.

data_flows.name: read telemetry
data_flows.description: The dashboard reads telemetry over BigQuery.

trust_boundaries.name: customer site
trust_boundaries.description: A customer-controlled site where sensor nodes are installed and serviced.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: sensor nodes installed on customer sites

trust_boundaries.name: internet
trust_boundaries.description: The internet-facing network through which sensor nodes connect to the device gateway and the firmware bucket is publicly readable.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: expose to the internet because the nodes dial in from anywhere

trust_boundaries.name: analytics network
trust_boundaries.description: The network containing the telemetry normalizer and telemetry processing stores.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: a Python consumer in our analytics network

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The corporate network from which fleet operators access dashboards.

assumptions.assumption: The customer site is a tenant-controlled trust zone because the sensor nodes are installed on customer sites and are outside our physical control.
assumptions.basis: The source says the nodes are installed on customer sites and are outside our physical control.

assumptions.assumption: The device registry is in the internet-facing device-gateway trust zone because the gateway accesses it and no separate registry zone is described.
assumptions.basis: The gateway looks up the device in the registry, while the source does not name a separate network zone for Firestore.

assumptions.assumption: Pub/Sub is in the analytics network because it carries readings to the telemetry normalizer and no separate Pub/Sub zone is described.
assumptions.basis: Pub/Sub is the intermediary between the device gateway and the consumer in the analytics network.

assumptions.assumption: The telemetry lake is confidential because it contains site addresses and occupancy patterns described as customer data.
assumptions.basis: The source says, "The lake has site addresses and occupancy patterns in it, so it is customer data."

assumptions.assumption: The Cloud Storage bucket is publicly readable and therefore classified as public.
assumptions.basis: The source explicitly says, "The bucket is public read."

assumptions.assumption: The Cloud Storage bucket is in the internet-facing trust zone because sensor nodes poll it remotely and it is public read; no separate storage zone is described.
assumptions.basis: The source says nodes poll the bucket and that it is public read, but names no separate network zone for it.

assumptions.assumption: The telemetry normalizer and telemetry lake carry business-critical telemetry data because the normalizer writes the platform's accepted readings into the lake.
assumptions.basis: The source describes the normalizer as the consumer that writes accepted readings into the telemetry lake.

assumptions.assumption: The dashboard is an internal process because fleet operators access it from the corporate network.
assumptions.basis: The source says fleet operators look at dashboards from the corporate network.
